en.html:
A day in the detention center is ruled by boredom.

Prison is another arrangement. There, the sentence is already settled. In a detention center they keep the unsentenced, plus those condemned prisoners who are treated as unsentenced (for them only one punishment is waiting, the final one, death, and nothing else), so forced labor is not done here.

On paper, a prisoner may volunteer for work. Permission exists; the arrangements do not. At Kanto Detention Center, therefore, the permitted request cannot be granted. Such was the guard's explanation.

Outside, in the open air, I may move about for thirty minutes per day. Only. All the remaining hours must be spent in silence inside the cell.

Reading and writing are allowed, but with limits. Neither will dispose of a whole long day.

So two options are left. Sleep without end. Alternatively—if one objects to sleeping one's body and mind into deterioration—take whatever exercise slightly more than two tatami will allow.

Loud noise is naturally not allowed. Equipment is also not allowed, even if you manufacture it from things already lying in the cell. Depending on the guard, even rubbing the body with a dry towel is read as preparation for strangling.

Practice swings are out of the question. Martial forms only scratch the guards' already frayed nerves for no benefit. In the end, what is possible is the standard muscle work: push-ups, sit-ups, back extensions.

In other words, exactly what I was doing at that moment.

ja.html:
拘置所の一日は退屈によって支配される。

　既に刑の確定した者のための施設である刑務所とは
異なり、拘置所に収容されるのは未決囚と未決囚扱い
の死刑囚（彼らに与えられるべき刑罰は最後の死のみ
であり、他には無い）なので、強制労働は行われない。

　規定の上では志願すれば労役に就くことも可能な筈
だが、この関東拘置所はその体制が整っていないため、
要望に応えることは不可能――とのことだった。
　看守からそう聞いている。

　外に出て体を動かせるのは一日あたり三十分間だけ。
　他の時間は全て独房内で静かに過ごさねばならない。

　読書や書き物は可能だが、制限がつく。
　長い一日を潰すのは無理だ。

　となれば後は、ひたすらに寝て過ごすか、あるいは
――貪眠による心身機能の低下を受容できないのなら
ば――二畳余の空間で許される限りの運動を行うしか
ない。

　派手な音を立てる行為は当然、認められない。
　器具を使うような運動も無論――例え獄室内にある
物で間に合わせるとしても。乾布摩擦でさえ、看守に
よっては絞殺の準備とみられる。

　素振りなどは論外。体術の型なども看守のささくれ
立った神経をいたずらに刺激するのみだ。
　結局のところ、出来ることは腕立て、腹筋、背筋と
いったスタンダードな筋トレの類に限られる。

　つまりは、俺が今している事もそれなのだった。

en.html:
Kageaki"Ji."
ｅｔｃ／看守"Notice has come. For questioning, you are being moved temporarily to Kamakura Police Station. The car is already here. You have ten minutes to get ready."
Kageaki"Understood."
ｅｔｃ／看守"...By the way, you."
Kageaki"Yes?"
ｅｔｃ／看守"What were you doing just now?"
Kageaki"Push-ups."
ｅｔｃ／看守"...Push-ups. I see."
Kageaki"Yes."
ｅｔｃ／看守"Where were you born?"
Kageaki"Nagasaki."
ｅｔｃ／看守"I am from Akita."
Kageaki"I hear the kiritanpo is excellent."
ｅｔｃ／看守"And Nagasaki has champon."
Kageaki"Yes."
ｅｔｃ／看守"...In my hometown, for push-ups we put both hands and both feet on the ground."
Kageaki"Generally, yes."
ｅｔｃ／看守"Push-up with the feet in the air, this is the first time I am seeing."
Kageaki"I have seldom observed anyone else doing them either."
ｅｔｃ／看守"Is it not painful?"
Kageaki"I writhe in agony."
ｅｔｃ／看守"...Good. That is a relief, actually."
Kageaki"I am glad to hear it."
ｅｔｃ／看守"Chalo, get ready."
Kageaki"Ji."

Kageaki"Muramasa holds the same view. Or rather... not one person escaped. It was total annihilation・・, literally. There is no room for misunderstanding."
Chief"Correct. Take the military meaning first. A unit loses the ability to function; we call it annihilated. The actual losses? Thirty to forty percent."
Chief"Annihilated, yet sixty percent survive. Nothing strange in that. But meet that thing・・, and even that sixty percent are not allowed to live."
Kageaki"Because it is not war. Between attacker and victim there is no such thing as combat, that lukewarm playful negotiation."
Kageaki"It is simply a natural disaster. A great tsunami hitting a coastal village. A great eruption hitting a village at the foot of the mountain. Survivors are not permitted to exist."

en.html:
A fact I state as a fact. No reply came.

On the east wall of the not-so-large room hangs one painting. Mulberry cultivation: an entirely ordinary landscape. Nothing in the technique calls for particular admiration either. As a matter of taste, however, I liked it.

It is not the work of any famous person. Not even a painter's. The owner of this room painted it himself. Maybe because it is ordinary, it has a quality that settles the viewer. ...Maybe I am being partial.

That painting is the only thing in this room one could call decoration. The rest is practical furniture, many documents, and assorted things with no taste and no charm.

For the head of the police station that is supposed to keep Kamakura's peace, a lonely arrangement. With a little more ambition in the matter of irony, I might call it <ruby>deplorable<rt>・・・・・</rt></ruby>.

Or <ruby>realistic<rt>・・・</rt></ruby>.

The realistic chief of this realistic office takes his eyes off the grain of the table and looks at me again.

ja.html:
事実を事実として言い切る。
　返答はなかった。

　広くもない室内の東側の壁に、絵が一幅、飾られて
いる。桑の栽培の様子を描いた、ごくごく平凡な風景
画だ。技術的にも見るべき点は特にないだろう。
　だが好悪を問うなら、好みだった。

　著名人の作品ではない。いや、画家の手になるもの
でさえない。それはこの部屋の主の、自筆だった。
　凡庸な作品だからこそと言うべきか、見る人を落ち
着かせるような趣がある。……贔屓目かもしれないが。

　そんな絵だけが、この部屋にあって唯一、装飾品と
呼べるものだった。
　後は実用本位の家具と多くの資料類、味も素っ気も
ない諸々があるばかりだ。

　鎌倉市の治安を預かる――べき――警察署の首長が
座すにしては、寂しい佇まいだと言えた。
　もう少し皮肉な表現力を駆使するなら、<ruby>嘆かわしい<rt>・・・・・</rt></ruby>
佇まいだと評することも可能かもしれない。

　あるいは<ruby>現実的<rt>・・・</rt></ruby>か。
　現実的な署長室の現実的な警察署長は、テーブルの
木目に向けていた視線を外し、再びこちらを見やって
いる。

Chief"You stopped the ‘egg’ from hatching."
Kageaki"Yes. We confirmed that Ukyo Nagasaka, the Rokuhara magistrate, and his mercenary Kotaro Fuma were both hosts. I killed them both."
Chief"At present, that is the most vital point. Let that thing multiply・・, and where will we be?"
Chief"Good work."
Kageaki"No. The one who suffered was never me."
Chief"...Hm. Did you get any information on Silver Star?"
Kageaki"Nothing from Ukyo Nagasaka. Kotaro Fuma seems to have had some conversation-level contact with it・・, but nothing meaningful, like its location, was obtained."
Chief"I see. Somebody, somewhere, must be protecting・・ it. That is how it should be viewed, but..."
Kageaki"Without that assumption, the facts do not balance."
Chief"A nationwide search is out for it as a missing person, and still nothing catches. Police weakness may be one reason, but..."
Chief"Two years now. Some supporter must be there; that is the conclusion to draw."
Kageaki"Quite so. But the purpose I cannot guess at all. Who would lend a hand to a killer who harms everyone, and why?"
Chief"Exactly. The logic will not hold, will it? ...Unfortunately, the world does a great deal of business without consulting logic."
Kageaki"In that case, to approach the truth by logical inference alone is difficult."
Chief"Correct. Sit comfortably, play detective—nothing will come of it."
Chief"Decisive information is needed. Sorry to ask, but I am counting on you, Kageaki."
Kageaki"Understood. Separately, one more matter is bothering me."
Chief"What is it?"
Kageaki"The man who supplied Kotaro Fuma with sword-armor. Name, Ichizo Sorimachi. He belongs to the Nogiyama Group, which Rokuhara employs, and he is also an errand boy for GHQ."
Chief"Ah..."
Kageaki"If I swallow every word I was told, Fuma got back sword-armor that GHQ had seized, through Sorimachi's arrangements. Why was such a thing permitted?"
Kageaki"The results of GHQ's sword-armor-hunting policy must surely be under strict seal. Otherwise, all the trouble of hunting and collecting sword-armor has no meaning."
Chief"...The teacher from the other day. Ryoubu Suzukawa. He also had sword-armor of unknown origin, didn't he?"
Kageaki"Yes. A connection is suspected."
Chief"How do you see it?"
Kageaki"...The reasonable inference would be: GHQ takes no interest in Yamato; the Occupation Army's discipline consequently slackens; supplies are easily diverted. Something of that order."
Chief"And the marks? Grade your own answer."
Kageaki"Fail."
Chief"Why?"
Kageaki"Is GHQ indifferent to Yamato?"
Chief"No. ...Yes, exactly that."
Chief"I already have a conjecture on this matter. But we will talk tomorrow. It will come up anyway, and I do not want to say this kind of thing many times."
Kageaki"Tomorrow?"
Chief"Rest tonight at my official residence. You need not go back to the detention center. Tomorrow, after work, there is a place I want you to accompany me."
Kageaki"Where to?"
Chief"Hachimangu. His Imperial Highness wishes to meet you."
Kageaki"..."
Kageaki"Why is that?"
Chief"His Highness worries about you more than you think. He takes the Silver Star affair, which harms so many citizens, as his own burden."
Chief"He expects much of you. For some time now, in fact, he has wanted to speak with you in person."
Kageaki"But. A body drenched in the pollution of blood, before the imperial house—"
Chief"His Highness is not a man to fuss over such petty things."
Kageaki"I do not think it petty. Those who preside over the altars of the state should stay far from impurity."
Chief"Now, do not make it difficult. His Highness is a practical man. He wants the facts from someone who was there. For that, who is there but you?"
Chief"That is all. So no need to charm anybody. Just answer His Highness's questions about the case."
Chief"Not quite an hour. Supply that much patience and come along."
Kageaki"...Understood."

Kageaki"Yes. We confirmed that Ukyo Nagasaka, the Rokuhara magistrate, and his mercenary Kotaro Fuma were both hosts. I killed them both."

Chief"At present, that is the most vital point. Let that thing multiply・・, and where will we be?"

Chief"Good work."

Kageaki"No. The one who suffered was never me."

Chief"...Hm. Did you get any information on Silver Star?"

Kageaki"Nothing from Ukyo Nagasaka. Kotaro Fuma seems to have had some conversation-level contact with it・・, but nothing meaningful, like its location, was obtained."

Chief"I see. Somebody, somewhere, must be protecting・・ it. That is how it should be viewed, but..."

Kageaki"Without that assumption, the facts do not balance."

Chief"A nationwide search is out for it as a missing person, and still nothing catches. Police weakness may be one reason, but..."

Chief"Two years now. Some supporter must be there; that is the conclusion to draw."

Kageaki"Quite so. But the purpose I cannot guess at all. Who would lend a hand to a killer who harms everyone, and why?"

Chief"Exactly. The logic will not hold, will it? ...Unfortunately, the world does a great deal of business without consulting logic."

Kageaki"In that case, to approach the truth by logical inference alone is difficult."

Chief"Correct. Sit comfortably, play detective—nothing will come of it."

Chief"What is it?"

Chief"Ah..."

ja.html:
署長 「〝卵〟の孵化は阻止したのだな」
景明 「はい。 　六波羅代官長坂右京とその傭兵風魔小太郎 が寄生体であることを確認、両名を殺害しま した」
署長 「現状で何よりも肝要なのはそこだ。 　あんなものに増え・・られては堪らん」
署長 「御苦労だったな」
景明 「いいえ。 　苦しんだのは決して、自分ではありません から」
署長 「…………。 　銀星号について情報は得られたか？」
景明 「長坂右京からは何も。 　風魔小太郎の方はあれ・・と会話程度の接触は した様子ですが、所在などの有意義な情報は やはり得られませんでした」
署長 「そうか。 　あれは何処かに、何者かが、保護・・している とみるべきなのだが……」
景明 「そう考えなくては、理屈に合いません」
署長 「失踪者扱いで全国に捜索を手配しているに も拘わらず、まるで引っ掛からないのだから な。 　警察力の不足もあるだろうが……」
署長 「もう二年にもなる。 　支援者がいると考えるべきだ」
景明 「全くに。しかし、目的が皆目わかりません。 　誰もを害する殺戮者に、誰がどうして手を 貸すのか」
署長 「ああ。筋道が通らんな？ 　……そして世の中、筋道の通らん話が割合 横行するから困る」
景明 「であれば、論理的推察のみによって真実へ 近付くのは難しいという事になります」
署長 「その通りだ。 　安楽椅子の探偵を気取っていてもどうにも ならん」
署長 「決定的な情報が要る。 　済まないが宜しく頼むぞ、景明」
景明 「承知しています。 　ところで。それとは別件で一つ、気になる 事柄が」
署長 「なんだ？」
景明 「風魔小太郎に劔冑を提供した男です。 　名は雪車町一蔵。六波羅御雇の野木山組に 属し、且つＧＨＱの御用聞きでもある」
署長 「ああ……」
景明 「自分が聞かされた話をすべて鵜呑みにする なら、という前提ですが――風魔はＧＨＱに 奪われた劔冑を雪車町の手配りで取り戻して いる。何故、そのような真似が許されたのか」
景明 「ＧＨＱの〝劔冑狩り〟政策の成果は当然、 厳重に封印されている筈。 　でなければ、手間隙を費やして劔冑を狩り 集めた意味がありません」
署長 「…………。 　先日の教師。鈴川令法か。彼も出所不明の 劔冑を持っていたのだったな」
景明 「はい。 　関連性が疑われます」
署長 「お前はどう考えている？」
景明 「……妥当な推論をするなら。 　ＧＨＱの大和への無関心が進駐軍の綱紀を 緩ませ、物資の横流しを安易に行わせている ――というあたりでしょう」
署長 「その推論に対する自己採点は？」
景明 「不可」
署長 「なぜ？」
景明 「ＧＨＱは大和に無関心ですか？」
署長 「否。 　……そう、そういうことだな」
署長 「この件については既に推測を持っている。 　だが、明日話そう。どうせ話題になる…… こんな話は幾度も口にしたくない」
景明 「明日？」
署長 「今日は私の役宅で休んでおけ。拘置所には 戻らなくていい。 　明日、仕事が済んだ後で付き合って欲しい 所がある」
景明 「どちらへ」
署長 「八幡宮だ。 　親王殿下がお前に会いたがっておられる」
景明 「…………」
景明 「それはまた、何故」
署長 「お前が思っている以上に、殿下はお前の事 を気に掛けておられるよ。 　殿下は国民を多く害する銀星号事件を我が 身の事として考えておいでだ」
署長 「お前にかける期待も大きい。 　一度親しく言葉を交わしたいと、実は前々 から仰せであった」
景明 「しかし。 　血の穢れに塗れた身を皇族の御前には――」
署長 「そんなつまらん事にこだわられる殿下では ない」
景明 「つまらぬ事とは思われません。 　社稷を司る者は不浄を遠ざけるべき」
署長 「まあ、そう言うな。 　要は実際的な方なのだよ、殿下は。事件の 実情を知るために現場の者の声を聞きたいと 望んでおられる。となればお前しかいない」
署長 「それだけだ。だから別に、愛想を振りまく 必要もない。 　事件について殿下の御下問にお答えすれば 済む」
署長 「小一時間ほどの辛抱だ。我慢して付き合え」
景明 「……わかりました」

en.html:
I nod, since I have no choice. A heavy matter, but once it is put like this, nothing else can be done.

—The prince at Hachimangu. I had heard the rumor that he is an oddball of the imperial family; apparently the rumor is true, or even an understatement. A noble who wants to meet a prisoner, such a thing I have never heard.

...I only hope he does not question me down to every last particular.

I drain the bowl, which gives no steam now. Tea that has lost its warmth is needlessly bitter.

en.html:
We leave Kamakura Police Station by the staff gate, and come out onto the street.

The chief has personally come to see me off. I am grateful for the kindness, but I worry about the eyes of people. A police chief seeing off a detainee is a strange picture.

Then again, the chief is in police uniform, while I am not wearing detention-center clothes. I knew the worry was useless.

en.html:
The chief's gaze suddenly drifts. Behind me, diagonally to the right.

Following it, I turn.

There is a figure.

Leaning her back on the concrete wall, she watches us sideways, head slightly lowered. At first sight, an indifferent attitude. But behind the eyes there is a fierce will.

As she was always, as far as I know.

A face strongly printed on my memory. Remembering her full name cost me no effort.
